newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagreb indicts senior Yugoslav Army officer.
newsitem.headline: Zagreb indicts senior Yugoslav Army officer.

text.p: Croatia has indicted the Chief-of-Staff of the Yugoslav Army for war crimes he allegedly committed as a colonel in the former federal Yugoslavia's army (JNA), Slobodna Dalmacija daily reported on Saturday.
The state prosecutor's office in the Adriatic port of Zadar on Friday accused Momcilo Perisic of war crimes against the city's civilian population.
Perisic was the commander of a JNA artillery tranining centre, from which big guns pounded the city during the Serb minority's rebellion against Croatia's independence in 1991.
The Serbs, backed by the JNA, seized a third of Croatia's territory by January 1992, when a ceasefire was signed. Zagreb recaptured the Serb-held enclaves in two lightning offensives in 1995.
Another 18 ex-JNA officers were also charged with issuing orders to bomb civilian targets in Zadar in September and October 1991.

"Perisic...issued orders to his (subordinates) to fire at precisely defined targets in Zadar and its surroundings from tanks, guns and other weapons," the daily quoted the state prosecutor's statement.
It did not say if Perisic would be tried in absentia.
The state news agency Hina said on Friday 30 people had died and over 120 buildings suffered considerable damage in attacks ordered by Perisic and his aides.
Croatia holds in custody only one of the 19 officers, now a senior Bosnian army commander. He was arrested in August at a border crossing with Italy and placed in a Zadar prison.
